editorNote: This issue catches late October 1982 as home-computer magazines teach readers to turn machines into games, while the mass market around them is all cartridges, arcade conversions, First Blood at the theater, and Jack & Diane on the radio.
morningLine: On the radio, John Cougar holds No. 1; at theaters, First Blood opens ahead of Halloween III; on the computer shelf, October magazines keep game programming, Atari reviews, and Commodore 64 notes in front of new owners.

lead.headline: Fall Shelves Turn Games Into Computer Lessons
lead.summary: The October computer-magazine rack makes the clearest personal-computing story for this week: game making and game playing sit beside memory maps, reviews, and utility software. COMPUTE! is selling readers on the idea that a home computer is not only a console substitute, but a machine to type into, tune, and understand.
lead.confidence: October 1982 magazine issue used as same-month shelf context for the week of October 18-24

market.headline: A Crowded Fall Counter for Machines and Games
market.summary: The late-October counter is split between practical business software, magazine-taught programming, and the entertainment pull of cartridges and arcade-style computer games. The home computer is being sold as both a tool and a toy.

bbsNote.headline: Modem Desk: Telegaming Enters the Vocabulary
bbsNote.summary: COMPUTE! listed a telecommunications item titled "Telegaming," a period reminder that games and modems were already being imagined together before home networking was common.

curiosity.headline: At the Movies: E.T. Retakes the Weekend
curiosity.summary: For the October 15 weekend, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial led the domestic box office, narrowly ahead of An Officer and a Gentleman, with My Favorite Year in third.

briefs.headline: First Blood Opens at No. 1
briefs.summary: The October 22 domestic weekend chart put First Blood first, followed closely by Halloween III: Season of the Witch.

briefs.headline: Jack & Diane Holds No. 1
briefs.summary: John Cougar led the Billboard Hot 100 dated October 23, 1982, with Men at Work, the Alan Parsons Project, Michael McDonald, and Joe Cocker & Jennifer Warnes filling out the top five.

briefs.headline: C64 Technical Notes Stay Timely
briefs.summary: A Commodore 64 memory-map article in COMPUTE! shows early owners needing practical maps of the new machine.
